reasoning: The September 2011 meeting introduced 'Operation Twist' — a concrete $400 billion maturity extension program purchasing 6-to-30-year Treasuries while selling an equal amount of shorter-term securities — representing the introduction of a new, named balance-sheet composition tool not present in August. Additionally, the reinvestment policy was materially changed from reinvesting agency principal payments into Treasury securities to reinvesting them into agency MBS, a distinct operational shift. Together these constitute the introduction of a new active policy program, qualifying as a major pivot under the definition of 'Introduction or termination of a QE/QT program.'
key_quote: The Committee intends to purchase, by the end of June [masked number of year] $400 billion of Treasury securities with remaining maturities of 6 years to 30 years and to sell an equal amount of Treasury securities with remaining maturities of 3 years or less.
